messages:
Anand: Heads up  need help. I got a denial for an out-of-network lab claim from last month (provider billed as OON) but the provider is actually in-network per the online directory. Claim ID CLM-88763. Anyone familiar with how to get this corrected?

Priya (People Ops): Sorry about that, Anand. Quick checklist: did you use the in-network facility address and your active member ID when they billed? Sometimes match fails if the TIN or provider name doesn't match the carrier's record.

Anand: I used the clinic's address and my member ID (A987654321). The denial reason says "provider not in network" and copay charged $120.

Benefits - Rahul: If the provider is listed on the insurer's directory but billed under a different practice name/TIN, we can file an appeal and include proof of in-network status. Please forward the explanation of benefits (EOB) and a screenshot of the insurer directory showing the provider as in-network. We'll submit the appeal as an urgent reconsideration and request an adjustment.

BenefitsBot:  Ticket created: #BEN-4533  "Appeal: OON denial but provider shows in-network". Expected response time: 2 business days. Attach EOB and screenshot to BEN-4533 or reply here.

Anand: Uploaded EOB and screenshot to the ticket. Also, is there anything I should ask the provider billing team to change?

Priya (People Ops): Ask the provider to resubmit claim with the correct practice/TIN and include your member ID and the insurer's preferred billing address. If they won't resubmit, we can escalate with the carrier directly. We'll track this and update you when the appeal is submitted.
